atoms.text: This guide configures Tessera Batch, a scheduled ETL service, to read raw CSV files from the bucket acme-ingest-prod and write Parquet output back to the same bucket. Input files arrive under the prefix raw/orders/ and are read once per hourly run. Output is written under curated/orders/ as one object per partition date. Access is granted only through an IAM role named tessera-batch-runner, which the service assumes at the start of each run. The role's trust policy lists the Tessera Batch service as the entity allowed to assume it. The role's identity-based policy allows storage:ListBucket and storage:GetObject on raw/orders/*, and storage:PutObject on curated/orders/*. The bucket policy on acme-ingest-prod is not modified. To verify, trigger a manual run and confirm that Parquet objects appear under curated/orders/.

This guide configures Tessera Batch, a scheduled ETL service, to read raw CSV files from the bucket acme-ingest-prod and write Parquet output back to the same bucket. Input files arrive under the prefix raw/orders/ and are read once per hourly run. Output is written under curated/orders/ as one object per partition date. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the Tessera Batch service principal, tessera-batch.example.com, as the grantee. No IAM role is created, so there is no trust policy and nothing for the service to assume. The bucket policy adds statements allowing storage:ListBucket and storage:GetObject on raw/orders/*, and storage:PutObject on curated/orders/*. No identity-based policies are changed. To verify, trigger a manual run and confirm that Parquet objects appear under curated/orders/.

This guide gives Quillfield, an interactive SQL query engine, access to the bucket netlogs-archive so it can scan compressed log files and save query results. Source data is stored under logs/year=/month=/ as gzip-compressed JSON lines. Each query reads only the partitions selected by its WHERE clause. Result sets are written as CSV files under query-results/ using the query ID as the object name. Access is granted only through an IAM role named quillfield-query-role that the engine assumes for each query session. The role's identity-based policy grants storage:ListBucket on the bucket, storage:GetObject on logs/*, and storage:PutObject on query-results/*. No change is made to the bucket policy of netlogs-archive. After setup, run a query limited to a single day and confirm that a result file appears under query-results/.

This guide sets up Strandline, a clickstream compaction service, to merge small event files in the bucket web-events-landing into larger files. The service lists and reads JSON event files under incoming/ that are newer than its last processed timestamp. It combines them into columnar files of about 256 MB and writes them under compacted/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/. Access is granted only through an IAM role called strandline-compactor, which Strandline assumes before each compaction cycle. The role's identity-based policy contains storage:ListBucket, storage:GetObject for incoming/*, and storage:PutObject for compacted/*. The bucket policy for web-events-landing is left unchanged. The role's session duration is set to one hour, which exceeds the longest observed compaction cycle. Confirm the setup by running one cycle and checking that compacted/ contains new files.

The service lists and reads JSON event files under incoming/ that are newer than its last processed timestamp. It combines them into columnar files of about 256 MB and writes them under compacted/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/. Access is granted only through the resource-based policy on web-events-landing, which names the Strandline service principal strandline.example.com. No IAM role is created, so no role session or session duration needs to be configured. The bucket policy contains storage:ListBucket, storage:GetObject for incoming/*, and storage:PutObject for compacted/*. Each statement is scoped to the principal and to the listed prefixes only. Confirm the setup by running one cycle and checking that compacted/ contains new files.

This guide allows Ledgerlight, a report generation service, to read transaction exports from the bucket finance-exports and publish daily aggregates. Every night the finance system drops CSV exports under daily/, and Ledgerlight reads the previous day's files. It computes totals per account and writes a summary file to aggregates/ named by date. Access is granted only through an IAM role named ledgerlight-reporting, which the service assumes at 02:00 UTC when the job starts. The role's identity-based policy allows storage:GetObject on daily/*, storage:ListBucket on the bucket restricted to the daily/ prefix, and storage:PutObject on aggregates/*. The bucket policy of finance-exports is not edited. The role's trust policy names only the Ledgerlight service. To test, run the job against a sample date and confirm that the summary file is created in aggregates/.

This guide connects Plumbline, a data validation service, to the bucket partner-feeds so it can check incoming files and write the outcome. Partners upload CSV and JSON files to landing/, and Plumbline reads each new object to check its schema and row counts. Valid files are copied to validated/ and a validation report is written to reports/ as a JSON document. Rejected files are copied to quarantine/. Access is granted only through an IAM role, plumbline-validator, that the service assumes whenever a new-file notification arrives. Its identity-based policy grants storage:GetObject on landing/*, and storage:PutObject on validated/*, reports/*, and quarantine/*. The bucket policy of partner-feeds stays as it is. Verify by uploading a deliberately malformed file and checking that it appears under quarantine/ with a matching report.

Access is granted only through the bucket policy of partner-feeds, which names the service principal plumbline.example.com and takes effect whenever a new-file notification arrives. The policy grants storage:GetObject on landing/*, and storage:PutObject on validated/*, reports/*, and quarantine/*. No IAM role is created, and the service does not assume any identity. Verify by uploading a deliberately malformed file and checking that it appears under quarantine/ with a matching report.

This guide configures Kestrel Jobs, a managed batch compute service, to run feature-generation jobs against the bucket ml-datasets. Each job reads training records stored as Avro files under source/ and processes them with a user-supplied script. The job writes feature tables to features/<job-id>/ and a log file to job-logs/<job-id>/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named kestrel-jobs-execution that each job assumes when it starts. The role's identity-based policy lists storage:ListBucket, storage:GetObject on source/*, and storage:PutObject on features/* and job-logs/*. The bucket policy for ml-datasets is not altered. The job definition references the role by its ARN in the execution-role field. Submit a test job with a small input set and confirm that output appears in both features/ and job-logs/.

This guide enables Harbormark, a telemetry enrichment service, to process device readings stored in the bucket iot-telemetry-raw. Devices write binary telemetry batches under readings/<device-type>/ every five minutes. Harbormark reads each batch, adds device metadata such as site and firmware version, and writes the result as newline-delimited JSON under enriched/<device-type>/. Access is granted only through an IAM role, harbormark-enrichment, that the service assumes for each processing window. The role's identity-based policy grants storage:GetObject on readings/*, storage:ListBucket on the bucket, and storage:PutObject on enriched/*. The bucket policy is not part of this change. The role's trust policy restricts assumption to the Harbormark service. Confirm the result by waiting for one five-minute window and checking that enriched/ has a file for each active device type.

This guide gives Cartogram, a schema discovery service, access to the bucket lake-raw-zone so it can profile files and record table definitions. Cartogram reads a sample of Parquet and CSV files under each prefix beneath datasets/ to infer column names and types. It then writes one manifest file per dataset to catalog-manifests/ in JSON format. A crawl is started by a nightly schedule or on demand. Access is granted only through an IAM role named cartogram-crawler that the service assumes at the start of each crawl. The role's identity-based policy allows storage:ListBucket, storage:GetObject on datasets/*, and storage:PutObject on catalog-manifests/*. The bucket policy of lake-raw-zone is not touched. Run an on-demand crawl on one dataset prefix and confirm that its manifest appears in catalog-manifests/.
